title: dep-scan evidence record
description: One record of the scan directory's evidence.jsonl: what a reachability producer said about one package, kept as the producer gave it. Nothing is inferred from advisory text and no record carries a timestamp. The id is ev- plus the first 16 hex digits of the SHA-256 digest over the canonical JSON of the array [schema version, producer name, kind, comparable subject purls sorted, [file, line, method] of the first location, discriminator], where the discriminator is the producer's own object id for the report object, or its MD5 content hash when the report names none; the documented algorithm is in analysis_lib.evidence. When two records' ids still collide after truncation, the store appends -2, -3 in canonical-JSON order. The examples array carries the three producer shapes the store was designed around: a blint presence record, a cdxgen occurrence record and a tracebom runtime-trace record.

schemaVersion.description: The record shape version. Every record of this shape carries 1.

id.description: The record id: ev- plus 16 lowercase hex digits of SHA-256 over the documented identity array, optionally followed by the store's collision suffix (-2, -3 and so on) when two records truncated to the same id.

producer.description: The tool that produced the record, with the tool version and the report schema version the record was read from.

kind.description: What the producer said. reached-flow, usage, callsite, entry-point and exploit-chain come from the reachability tools; occurrence, callstack, annotation and introspection come from BOM production; presence and runtime-trace come from binary and runtime analysis; sanitizer, dead-code, dependency and no-path record negative or non-reaching evidence; weakness and dangerous-api are a producer's own weakness candidates and its reachable calls into dangerous APIs, kept as given and never counted as reached.

polarity.description: positive when the record says the subject was observed or reached; negative when it says the opposite, such as a sanitizer on the path or a package the trace showed is not reached.

subject.description: The package or component the record is about. The purls array may be empty for records that are about a place rather than a package, such as an entry point with no package resolved.

locations.description: Where the evidence lives, relative to the scanned source root with forward slashes.

items.description: One witness node on the path.

path.description: The witness path the producer walked, in its order, at most 64 nodes. When the producer gave more, the first 64 are kept and a path-truncated caveat is added.

confidence.description: The producer's own confidence value, exactly as it wrote it, for example High, high or 0.87. Absent when the producer states none; dep-scan never invents one.

items.description: One thing to discount or know about this record.

caveats.description: The caveats that apply to this record: a budget or timeout the producer hit, a schema drift, a path that was cut, an object of the report that could not become a record. Empty when there is nothing to flag.

source.description: The scan-directory-relative file the record was read from, with forward slashes, for example python-reachables.slices.json or analysis/dosai/dotnet-dataflows.json.

attributes.description: Everything else the producer stated about the object, kept as given: reach fields, rule ids, taint kinds, service purls, exposure tiers, chain ids. A later grader reads what it needs from here; dep-scan adds nothing.

producer.description: The tool that produced the record, as it names itself.

name.description: Producer name, for example atom, golem, rusi, dosai, kosi, blint, cdxgen or tracebom.

version.description: The producer tool's own version, for example 4.0.2 for atom 4.0.2.

reportSchemaVersion.description: The version the report names for itself, a shape-implied version when the report carries none, or the literal string unknown.

items.description: One package URL, kept as the producer gave it.

purls.description: The package URLs the record is about, deduplicated and comparable by the comparable-purl rule.

componentRef.description: The BOM component bom-ref the adapter resolved for the subject, present only when one was resolved.

location.description: One place the evidence lives, relative to the scanned source root with forward slashes.

file.description: The file path, relative to the scanned source root with forward slashes.

line.description: Line number in file, counting from 1.

method.description: The enclosing method or function name, when the producer resolved one.

path-node.description: One witness node of a path: a frame the producer walked. Every field is optional because producers describe different subsets.

file.description: The file path, relative to the scanned source root with forward slashes.

line.description: Line number in file, counting from 1.

method.description: The method or function name at this node.

symbol.description: The fully qualified symbol the producer named at this node.

caveat.description: One thing a reader should discount or know: a budget the producer hit, a schema that drifted, a path that was cut, a record that could not be built.

kind.description: budget and timeout when the producer stopped early; collapsed-edges and unresolved-call-sites when the producer's own analysis was imprecise; coverage-gap when a part of the scan had no analysis; path-truncated when a witness path was cut at 64 nodes; schema-minor for a newer minor report version; schema-unknown for a report that names no version; minimal-api for an entry point whose attribution the producer may have misplaced; record-skipped for a producer object that could not become a record; location-outside-root for a file the producer named outside the scanned source root, which the record leaves out rather than carry as an absolute path.

detail.description: What exactly happened, in one sentence a reader can act on.
